units.source_text: 有的情人，利用信鸽充当他们爱的使者。

en.t: Some lovers use carrier pigeons as messengers of their love.

units.source_text: 男方外出旅行，怎么能够让鸽子从他到达的遥远的地方飞回女方的住所呢？

en.t: When the man goes away on a journey, how can he make the pigeon fly back from the faraway place he has reached to the woman's home?

units.source_text: 这是由于情人相信系在鸽子腿上的情书有一种爱的力量吧。

en.t: Perhaps it is because lovers believe that a love letter tied to a pigeon's leg has a kind of power of love.

units.source_text: 许多时候，各种动物要比人更敏锐地预知人的命运。

en.t: Often, all sorts of animals foresee human fate more keenly than people do.

units.source_text: 记得我曾告诉过你，我孩提时，父亲在伊豆的山中打猎，丢了一只大猎犬。

en.t: I remember telling you once that when I was a child, my father went hunting in the mountains of Izu and lost a large hunting dog.

units.source_text: 这只猎犬第八天才拖着瘦弱的身躯，摇摇摆摆地回到我们的家里。

en.t: Only on the eighth day did the dog drag its weakened body back to our house, staggering as it came.

units.source_text: 这只猎犬除了主人以外，什么人给东西它都不吃。

en.t: That hunting dog would not eat anything given to it by anyone except its master.

units.source_text: 它凭借什么力量从伊豆走回东京来的呢？

en.t: By what power did it walk back from Izu to Tokyo?
